patchNotes.title: Indonesian Translation (Early Access)
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.72.0-PB - Indonesian Translation (Early Access)
patchNotes.excerpt: 🇮🇩 Hello Indonesia! We’re happy to announce the early access release of the first translated language for IdleMMO: Indonesian. For new players, the game will automatically display in Indonesian. Existing players can...

contentBlocks.text: 🇮🇩 Hello Indonesia! We’re happy to announce the early access release of the first translated language for IdleMMO: Indonesian.
For new players, the game will automatically display in Indonesian. Existing players can enable it by navigating to Settings → Language.

Please note that this translation is AI-assisted and may contain occasional errors or awkward phrasing. Languages that are AI-assisted are clearly marked within the UI so players are aware that some issues may occur.
Certain areas of the game, such as dialogue and quests, have not yet been translated as we continue ironing out issues before scaling things up further.
We also plan to support more languages in the future, including fully human-curated translations. This is just the start, and the first of many languages to come.

patchNotes.title: Small Adjustments
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.71.0-PB - Small Adjustments
patchNotes.excerpt: House Repair Costs House component expiry has been increased from 60 days to 90 days for members, and from 45 days to 60 days for free players. This should help significantly reduce the burden of having to keep consta...

contentBlocks.text: House Repair Costs

House component expiry has been increased from 60 days to 90 days for members, and from 45 days to 60 days for free players. This should help significantly reduce the burden of having to keep constant repair of your buildings.
Your building will enter the new 60/90 day cycle the moment it has been repaired.
Combat Cap
We’ve reviewed the recent combat changes regarding the reduced 3 second cap. We’re confident in the direction of the update. As a result, the change will remain in the game.
This change will take effect at the next cycle.
League Changes

League generation has been tightened up so league schedules still feel random, but less chaotic. Normal players will now get more consistent access to core league types, especially battle leagues, while restricted leagues for Forsaken, Cursed, and Banished characters are capped more sensibly per cycle. The system will also avoid stacking multiple near-identical leagues for the same audience at the same time, reducing cases where one league is basically duplicated inside another.
More
Added button to the inventory to indicate that it's possible to purchase an extra slot.
Increased tavern shard reward to 25 daily/150 weekly.
We've updated our public road map which can be seen here: https://trello.com/b/CxIn7i5B/idlemmo-public-roadmap
Public API
Added guild energizing pool endpoint ( /v1/guild/{id}/energizing-pool/information ).
Added guild hall endpoint ( /v1/guild/{id}/hall ).
Added location endpoint with the weather forecast ( v1/world/locations/list ). All dates displayed are in UTC.
Added hashed_id to the guild members list.
Added full stat breakdown for individual pets.
Added total_experience to the pet endpoint.

patchNotes.title: Balancing Adjustments
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.70.2-PB - Balancing Adjustments
patchNotes.excerpt: We’ve made a few small tweaks to hunting and battle loot. As mentioned before, lowering the battle cap meant loot was coming in a bit quicker than intended. We're also continuing to fine-tune the balance between hunti...

contentBlocks.text: We’ve made a few small tweaks to hunting and battle loot.

As mentioned before, lowering the battle cap meant loot was coming in a bit quicker than intended. We're also continuing to fine-tune the balance between hunting and battling so that hunting feels more rewarding and worthwhile in its own right. We’ve been keeping an eye on things recently, and here’s what we’ve adjusted:
Base hunting speed has been increased by ~18%.
Loot chance for all enemies has been reduced to better align with the updated battle system.
Loot found while hunting has been increased by ~20%.
Enemies at the citadel differ in difficulty. We've increased the experience on some of those to represent that.

Hunting should now feel a bit faster overall, which helps smooth out the flow between hunting and battling. Since you're getting through enemies more quickly, the loot chance has been tuned down to keep things balanced.

There are a lot of moving parts here, as increasing hunting speed also indirectly impacts overall loot, and weather now plays into that as well. We'll keep an eye on how it all settles and make further adjust accordingly if needed.

patchNotes.headline: Version 0.70.1-PB - Bug Fixes

contentBlocks.text: Removed the ability to change the games contrast.
Updated how the brightness setting behaves.
UI scale now uses preset options instead of a % slider.

Certain devices were experiencing graphical rendering issues, particularly those using an Adreno GPU, which could cause screen tearing and graphical artifacts. This won't resolve every rendering issue, but a large portion of them were linked to the settings above.
If you have changed your brightness, or UI scaling in the past, you will need to go back to your settings and make the change again.
Bug Fixes
Fixed pet hunting in locations that are higher than your current characters combat level.

patchNotes.title: Weather, hunting changes, and much more
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.70.0-PB - Weather, hunting changes, and much more
patchNotes.excerpt: Weather Weather’s officially landed in IdleMMO. We've added weather to make the world feel a bit more alive, with things shifting based on both the current weather and the season. Sometimes that works in your favour,...

contentBlocks.text: Weather
Weather’s officially landed in IdleMMO.

We've added weather to make the world feel a bit more alive, with things shifting based on both the current weather and the season. Sometimes that works in your favour, sometimes it doesn’t, depending on how rough the conditions are.

For example, clear weather gives you a nice +10% hunting efficiency boost. On the flip side, something like a storm will hit you with -15% efficiency. But since it’s tougher, you’ll get a +35% experience bonus while hunting in those conditions. Efficiency is additive too, so you can offset some of the negatives with things like potions.

Weather isn’t global either. It changes depending on where you are, based on the area’s geography and the current season. So places like Skyreach Peak will be heavy on snow in winter, but ease up a bit in summer. Seasons follow real-world northern hemisphere dates, so winter runs from December through to the end of February, and so on.

It also affects which enemies you run into. Some creatures show up more often in certain weather, while others become harder to find. You can check exactly how each enemy reacts by looking them up in-game.
We have 9 weather types:
Clear - Favorable weather with improved efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining.
Overcast - Neutral weather.
Rain - Improves fishing efficiency, but reduces woodcutting and mining efficiency. Woodcutting and mining receive increased experience.
Fog - Reduces efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining, but grants increased experience for the affected activities.
Storm - Significantly reduces efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining, but grants strong experience bonuses for the affected activities.
Magic Storm - Rare weather that increases magic find for battles and world bosses.
Windy - Improves hunting efficiency, but reduces fishing and woodcutting efficiency. Fishing and woodcutting receive increased experience.
Snow - Reduces efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining, but grants increased experience for the affected activities.
Heatwave - Significantly reduces efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining, but grants increased experience for the affected activities.
This is just the start as well. The weather system is going to tie into more parts of the game over time, and it lays the groundwork for farming, which is on the way.
Hunting Loot
When hunting, you now have a small chance to find loot dropped by enemies. The rates are a bit on the lower side for now, but we’ll keep an eye on it and adjust things if it feels too stingy.
Power Hunting

We’ve reworked power hunting to feel a lot more engaging in short bursts, rather than something you have to grind through for ages. Before, it could feel a bit of a chore, especially since it was available often enough that skipping it felt like you were missing out.
Now it’s spaced out much more, and when you do jump in, it’s quicker, more interactive, and done in a few minutes.
Heres a quick breakdown:

Enemies show up roughly every second, so there’s a steady flow while you’re in it. Power hunting lasts up to 5 minutes, depending on your hunting mastery, so it’s short and focused. The experience from hunting mastery has been increased, now ranging from 4 to 25 instead of 1 to 15. On top of that, you can only do power hunting once every 10 to 12 hours, depending on your membership.

Because enemies appear faster and the experience has been bumped up, the overall rewards are significantly higher. It’s now something you can dip into, grab a solid chunk of experience, and move on without it taking over your play session.
We’ll keep monitoring how this feels and make further adjustments if needed. If it still feels like a grind despite it being shorter or just isn’t engaging, we’ll take a step back and rethink it.
Referrals
We’ve made a big update to the referral system.
Now, when you refer someone and they get membership for the first time, both of you will receive 2,500 shards each. This includes membership obtained entirely through in-game gold.
Guild Weapons
We’re putting a bit more focus on guild weapons, as the uptake has been a little lower than expected.
To help with that, we’ve removed the guild mark cost entirely when building weapons. It should make them much more accessible and easier to get into.
We’ll keep an eye on how this plays out and make further adjustments if needed.
More
Added Pet Mastery and Hunting Mastery leagues. These will be available after the next cycle is processed.
Replaced the boss action percentage with a timer during world boss battles.
Enemy scaling now automatically saves your last used settings.
You can now equip items directly from the equipment page.
Removed the toast pop-up when adding items to a trade, as it was covering parts of the UI.
Improved tapping on item rarity on mobile, making it easier to view how many are in circulation.
Added the ability to preview ascension perks.
Fixed an issue where tavern items wouldn’t fade out when opening a post on mobile.
Added clarification to the hunting page that hunting tracks enemies rather than battling them.
Fixed a bug that showed the market task on market locked characters.
Fixed a bug that caused the shrine to be stuck for 10 minutes after it resets.
Wiki

We're aware the wiki has fell behind in the last few updates and, as it stands, it remains outdated. We will take some time in the near future to make sure everything is up to date, including adding more detailed information about weather.

patchNotes.bodyText:
Weather
Weather’s officially landed in IdleMMO.
We've added weather to make the world feel a bit more alive, with things shifting based on both the current weather and the season. Sometimes that works in your favour, sometimes it doesn’t, depending on how rough the conditions are.
For example, clear weather gives you a nice +10% hunting efficiency boost. On the flip side, something like a storm will hit you with -15% efficiency. But since it’s tougher, you’ll get a +35% experience bonus while hunting in those conditions. Efficiency is additive too, so you can offset some of the negatives with things like potions.
Weather isn’t global either. It changes depending on where you are, based on the area’s geography and the current season. So places like Skyreach Peak will be heavy on snow in winter, but ease up a bit in summer. Seasons follow real-world northern hemisphere dates, so winter runs from December through to the end of February, and so on.
It also affects which enemies you run into. Some creatures show up more often in certain weather, while others become harder to find. You can check exactly how each enemy reacts by looking them up in-game.
We have 9 weather types:
Clear - Favorable weather with improved efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining.
Overcast - Neutral weather.
Rain - Improves fishing efficiency, but reduces woodcutting and mining efficiency. Woodcutting and mining receive increased experience.
Fog - Reduces efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining, but grants increased experience for the affected activities.
Storm - Significantly reduces efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining, but grants strong experience bonuses for the affected activities.
Magic Storm - Rare weather that increases magic find for battles and world bosses.
Windy - Improves hunting efficiency, but reduces fishing and woodcutting efficiency. Fishing and woodcutting receive increased experience.
Snow - Reduces efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining, but grants increased experience for the affected activities.
Heatwave - Significantly reduces efficiency for hunting, fishing, woodcutting, and mining, but grants increased experience for the affected activities.
This is just the start as well. The weather system is going to tie into more parts of the game over time, and it lays the groundwork for farming, which is on the way.
Hunting Loot
When hunting, you now have a small chance to find loot dropped by enemies. The rates are a bit on the lower side for now, but we’ll keep an eye on it and adjust things if it feels too stingy.
Power Hunting
We’ve reworked power hunting to feel a lot more engaging in short bursts, rather than something you have to grind through for ages. Before, it could feel a bit of a chore, especially since it was available often enough that skipping it felt like you were missing out.
Now it’s spaced out much more, and when you do jump in, it’s quicker, more interactive, and done in a few minutes.
Heres a quick breakdown:
Enemies show up roughly every second, so there’s a steady flow while you’re in it. Power hunting lasts up to 5 minutes, depending on your hunting mastery, so it’s short and focused. The experience from hunting mastery has been increased, now ranging from 4 to 25 instead of 1 to 15. On top of that, you can only do power hunting once every 10 to 12 hours, depending on your membership.
Because enemies appear faster and the experience has been bumped up, the overall rewards are significantly higher. It’s now something you can dip into, grab a solid chunk of experience, and move on without it taking over your play session.
We’ll keep monitoring how this feels and make further adjustments if needed. If it still feels like a grind despite it being shorter or just isn’t engaging, we’ll take a step back and rethink it.
Referrals
We’ve made a big update to the referral system.
Now, when you refer someone and they get membership for the first time, both of you will receive 2,500 shards each. This includes membership obtained entirely through in-game gold.
Guild Weapons
We’re putting a bit more focus on guild weapons, as the uptake has been a little lower than expected.
To help with that, we’ve removed the guild mark cost entirely when building weapons. It should make them much more accessible and easier to get into.
We’ll keep an eye on how this plays out and make further adjustments if needed.
More
Added Pet Mastery and Hunting Mastery leagues. These will be available after the next cycle is processed.
Replaced the boss action percentage with a timer during world boss battles.
Enemy scaling now automatically saves your last used settings.
You can now equip items directly from the equipment page.
Removed the toast pop-up when adding items to a trade, as it was covering parts of the UI.
Improved tapping on item rarity on mobile, making it easier to view how many are in circulation.
Added the ability to preview ascension perks.
Fixed an issue where tavern items wouldn’t fade out when opening a post on mobile.
Added clarification to the hunting page that hunting tracks enemies rather than battling them.
Fixed a bug that showed the market task on market locked characters.
Fixed a bug that caused the shrine to be stuck for 10 minutes after it resets.
Wiki
We're aware the wiki has fell behind in the last few updates and, as it stands, it remains outdated. We will take some time in the near future to make sure everything is up to date, including adding more detailed information about weather.

patchNotes.title: World Boss Changes
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.69.1-PB - World Boss Changes
patchNotes.excerpt: World bosses now take significantly longer to respawn after being defeated. For example, Isadora now respawns every 8 hours instead of every 2 hours. To match that, loot rates have been increased so each successful ba...

contentBlocks.text: World bosses now take significantly longer to respawn after being defeated. For example, Isadora now respawns every 8 hours instead of every 2 hours.

To match that, loot rates have been increased so each successful battle feels more rewarding. As a general rule, longer respawn times now come with better rewards, though not every drop has been adjusted in a strict one-to-one way. For example, the Wrex Egg has increased from 3% to 8.7%.

The main goal of this change is to make world bosses feel much less demanding, especially for more casual players. The shorter timers made it easy to feel like you had to keep checking in or risk missing out. With longer gaps between spawns and stronger rewards per boss, it should feel much easier to join in without needing to track every spawn throughout the day.
These changes only apply to the core world bosses. Seasonal bosses haven’t been adjusted yet, though we may revisit them before the next seasonal campaign.

We’ve also increased the time it takes to defeat a world boss. The original pacing was set much earlier in the game’s lifecycle, and it no longer lines up with the slower direction the game has moved towards over the past year.
More
World Bosses should no longer overlap and there is a 5 minute grace period between them.

Please Note Because of the above changes, if you've built a world boss timer that relies purely on calculating spawn times, you'll need to switch over to the public API. It's no longer possible to accurately predict exact world boss timings through calculation alone.

patchNotes.title: Battle Changes
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.69.0-PB - Battle Changes
patchNotes.excerpt: Battle Changes (Trial) We've reduced the battle time cap to 3 seconds and adjusted the battle formula. This is something we’ve been meaning to tackle for a while, and we’ve taken the opportunity to do it alongside som...

contentBlocks.text: Battle Changes (Trial)
We've reduced the battle time cap to 3 seconds and adjusted the battle formula.

This is something we’ve been meaning to tackle for a while, and we’ve taken the opportunity to do it alongside some of the recent quality-of-life work. We’ve reworked battle pacing so stronger characters can actually feel stronger again, without hitting that old hard 8-second cap. Before, once you got fast enough, everything just flattened out at 8 seconds and stopped feeling meaningful. Now, battle times scale down more naturally. You’ll still need strong stats to see the biggest gains, but progression at the high end should feel a lot smoother and more rewarding. At the same time, the fastest battles are still kept in check so the overall combat system stays stable.

Alongside that, we’ve slightly reduced hunting rates for both characters and pets. Pets have taken a bit more of a hit here, mainly because they can stack and gather enemies at the same time. This is to control the increased battle efficiency which affects areas like loot generation, conquest progress, and overall combat progression.

It’s also worth noting that there will be a small window where, under very specific circumstances, battles may be slightly slower than before the update. For most players who were previously hitting the 8-second cap though, battles should now feel noticeably faster.

We’re treating this as a trial until the end of the current guild season on 7th May . At that point, we’ll review it properly and decide whether to revert and go back to the drawing board, or keep it in place. So for now, it’s best to treat this as a limited-time test while we assess how it performs and decide on the right long-term direction.

We’ll be keeping a close eye on how things settle over the next few weeks, and we may make further adjustments if needed. This may include changes to the battle formula, loot, and hunting rates. Our ultimate goal is to move away from the 8-second cap and give stats and items more meaning, while making sure we don’t accidentally flood the game with too much new loot and causing wider issues.
More
Your battle stance will now be remembered and automatically selected based on your last choice.
Queued dungeon runs that haven’t started yet will now be refunded if you cancel your current dungeon action.
Tavern posts will now fade once viewed, as long as they haven’t been updated since you last opened them.
The Tavern reply box now expands automatically as you type.
You can now filter banished guilds.
Guild raid completion notifications now include the loot you received.

Fixed tavern rendering bugs on certain Android devices.
Giveaway (MS, DSS, Shards, Tokens)
If you haven't noticed yet, we're holding a huge giveaway in the tavern. 40 winners!
10× 30 Days Membership Pack (1 per winner)
10× Dragon Soulstone (1 per winner)
10× 1,000 Tokens (1 per winner)
10× 10,000 Shards (1 per winner)
That’s a total of 40 individual winners. Each user can only win once (regardless of character).
How To Enter
Simply make a post or reply anywhere in the tavern. That's it.

Every post or reply increases your chances of winning. Posts flagged as spam will not be counted. Posts in the game category also will not count. We use an internal spam scoring system, and any post below a certain threshold will be excluded. So don't be clever and try to game the system. Any attempts to do so will result in your entry being disqualified and a mute from the tavern.
See the tavern post in General for more information.
Character Name Clarification

With some character names becoming available soon due to the recent cleanup of older accounts, we want to clarify our stance on character name squatting. Creating or claiming character names in bad faith won't be tolerated. This includes taking names of well-known characters with the sole intention of selling them on for gold or items.

As a result, some adjustments were needed. We’ve updated the pricing and drop rates for Mythics in Eden’s Embrace, Arboreal Labyrinth, and Bloodmoon Manor. These dungeons had become clear outliers in terms of profitability*, largely due to their position as introductory Mythic dungeons.

The vendor value for tools have been increased. We’re aware this may impact dungeon profitability on those that drop tools, and we’ll be keeping a close eye on those for potential further adjustments. The affected tools were removed from the market prior to this update.

* For clarity, when we refer to profitability, we are specifically talking about the amount of gold generated by selling items to the vendor. This does not include the value or profit of items when they are sold or traded between players.
More
Posts in the gaming tavern category no longer count towards the shard goal.
The sale for Mythic pets in the Celestial Exchange will end when the Springtide Fair event concludes.
For more detail on the rationale behind these changes and our overall approach, please refer to our full blog post: https://www.galahadcreative.com/blog/idlemmo-economic-changes/

patchNotes.title: Tavern and Balancing Changes
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.68.0-PB - Tavern and Balancing Changes
patchNotes.excerpt: Tavern Improvements We've made general improvements to the tavern including UX and UI improvements. We've removed the gold cost for creating a topic. We've overhauled the spam detection system due to it being too stro...

contentBlocks.text: Tavern Improvements
We've made general improvements to the tavern including UX and UI improvements.
We've removed the gold cost for creating a topic.
We've overhauled the spam detection system due to it being too strong. You can now make responses without worrying about it being flagged as low quality.
The shard reward goal now only counts quality contributions.
We've increased the shard reward to 10 daily shards and 60 weekly shards.
Added a tavern homepage with a breakdown on the most recent posts + top commenters
More
Increased the housing component expiry cooldown from 30 days for free players and 40 days for members. To 45 days for free players, and 60 days for members.
Increased maximum construction efficiency bonus from levelling to 25% (from 20%).
Special items value have been increased to 500,000.
Dragon soul stones have been increased to 50,000.
Pet egg values have all received a significant increase.
To prevent issues or edge cases in the market, we have cleared the market and returned the adjusted items to the sellers inventory.

Coming Soon This is not the only balancing change planned. We still have further adjustments coming for dungeons and tools, and may also review and adjust other areas of the game, such as alchemy items, further down the line. Additional planned changes will be rolled out shortly after this update.

patchNotes.title: Inactive Account Deletion
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.67.2-PB - Inactive Account Deletion
patchNotes.excerpt: We’re introducing an account cleanup to remove inactive and low-progress accounts from the game. Guest accounts will be deleted after 30 days of inactivity. Registered accounts with a total level below 150 will be mar...

contentBlocks.text: We’re introducing an account cleanup to remove inactive and low-progress accounts from the game.
Guest accounts will be deleted after 30 days of inactivity.
Registered accounts with a total level below 150 will be marked for deletion if they’ve been inactive for more than 6 months .
Registered accounts with a total level below 250 will be marked for deletion if they’ve been inactive for more than 12 months.
Accounts with a total level of 250 or higher won’t be affected.

Registered accounts will be notified by email and will have 21 days from the notice to log in and reactivate their account. We expect this process to remove a large number of old accounts. As a result, many previously used usernames will become available again.
More
Fixed an issue with buildings not correctly completing in the background.
Fixed building cost breakdown not accounting for the characters construction level.

contentBlocks.text: Seasonal battles have been scheduled. Throw eggs at members of the opposing teams to obtain points for your team.
Quick Recap:
Seasonal battles are only available during specific, short-lived time periods. Any eggs thrown outside of these active windows will not count toward points.
Every egg successfully thrown at an opposing team during an active battle awards 3 points to the player’s team.
Throwing eggs at players on other teams also grants 10 experience toward the campaign-related skill. For example, landing a egg on an opposing team awards 10 Springtide Mastery experience.
Each egg thrown during a battle against an opposing team gives a 5% chance of receiving 1 to 5 shards.
Head over to the seasonal campaign page and press "Battles" to view any current or upcoming battles.
View the wiki page here for a more detailed breakdown: https://wiki.idle-mmo.com/campaigns/seasonal-contest

patchNotes.headline: Version 0.67.0-PB - Springtide Fair
patchNotes.excerpt: @@IMAGE:Springtide Fair Springtide Fair Is Here! Find hollow eggs, partake in scavenger hunts, and earn exclusive rewards in our seasonal Springtide Fair campaign. Head to the Springtide Fair location to unlock the ex...

contentBlocks.text: @@IMAGE:Springtide Fair
Springtide Fair Is Here!
Find hollow eggs, partake in scavenger hunts, and earn exclusive rewards in our seasonal Springtide Fair campaign.

Head to the Springtide Fair location to unlock the exclusive Springtide Mastery skill. Use this skill to collect seasonal items, which you can exchange for points on the campaign page to advance through the campaign.
Visit the merchants to discover brand-new skins!
Heads Up

As mentioned in the recent blog post, you can expect potential balancing changes across various areas of the game over the next few weeks as we continue reviewing overall balance. This may include areas such as tools, equipment, existing specials, potions, dragon soul stones, pet eggs, dungeon costs, and more.
The Construction skill will also be part of this review and may receive adjustments.
Nothing is final at this stage. Some areas may change during the review, while others may take longer or remain completely unchanged as we continue refining the approach.
As of writing, nothing is confirmed. This is a heads up in case you’re currently trading or holding items that could be impacted.
Before any changes do go live, any affected market listings will be removed and returned to your character if the value of the item increases.
You can view our lengthy rationale behind this here: https://www.galahadcreative.com/blog/idlemmo-economic-changes/
More
The efficiency obtained from leveling up construction doubled. It now scales from 0% to 20% according to your level instead of 0% to 10%.
Fixed paw icon on the pet showcase.
[Public API] Fixed the character pet endpoint not correctly returning the pets stats.

patchNotes.title: Economic Rationale
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.66.2-PB - Economic Rationale
patchNotes.excerpt: We’ve recently made a number of changes to vendor values across items, alongside the earlier adjustment to membership scroll pricing. With these changes, we wanted to take a step back and explain the thinking behind t...

contentBlocks.text: We’ve recently made a number of changes to vendor values across items, alongside the earlier adjustment to membership scroll pricing.

With these changes, we wanted to take a step back and explain the thinking behind them. The goal is to give a clear, high-level view of what’s been changing, why we’ve been doing it, and where we’re trying to take things.

By increasing vendor values, trades now carry a more meaningful cost, gold is removed more consistently through tax, and items have a stronger floor when it comes to pricing. It also adds a bit more weight to how items are transferred and used, which helps reduce some of the distortion we’ve been seeing around item movement and progression.

In the short term, the market may feel a bit unsettled as everything adjusts, which is to be expected. We’ll be keeping a close eye on how things behave over the coming weeks and making adjustments where needed.

Because our approach relies on letting the data come in, we can’t rule out further changes just yet. This could include things like increasing dungeon entry costs, lowering item drop rates, or adjusting item values if that ends up being the simplest option.

Things need time to settle before we have a clear picture of what’s actually happening. It’s also entirely possible that no further changes will be needed, but we need to give it that time before making the call. We’ll also be reviewing other areas of the game, such as egg drops, alchemy items, and Dragon Soulstones, so consider this a heads-up.
You can read our entire lengthy rationale here: https://www.galahadcreative.com/blog/idlemmo-economic-changes/

patchNotes.title: Item Value Increase
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.66.0-PB - Item Value Increase
patchNotes.excerpt: We have updated the vendor values for Legendary and Mythic forge items and their recipes to better match their actual value. These values were previously too low for the strength, rarity, and market demand of the item...

contentBlocks.text: We have updated the vendor values for Legendary and Mythic forge items and their recipes to better match their actual value.

These values were previously too low for the strength, rarity, and market demand of the items involved. As a result, high-end items could be traded for very little tax, moved between players too cheaply, and used in low-cost item lending or forging services more often than intended.
We don't want to eliminate these services entirely. However, one of our goals is to increase the barrier to entry so they require more meaningful investment to access.

To improve this, we reviewed current player market prices and used them as the main reference point when setting the new vendor values. Mythic values were adjusted more closely to active market pricing, while Legendary values were tuned more carefully due to the wider difference between weaker and stronger items in that tier.
This update is intended to:
Give high-end items and recipes a more appropriate vendor floor
Increase trade tax on powerful items so it better matches their value
Reduce cheap item loaning and temporary transfers
Make low-cost forging handoffs less attractive

patchNotes.headline: Version 0.64.0-PB - Construction (Houses)
patchNotes.excerpt: This update introduces Housing , a new system that allows you to extend the maximum idle time for various activities. Village Management has been postponed for now, as it required significantly more development time t...

contentBlocks.text: This update introduces Housing , a new system that allows you to extend the maximum idle time for various activities.
Village Management has been postponed for now, as it required significantly more development time than originally expected.

Important: This update includes major foundational changes to several core systems, particularly Guild Halls and primary skills. Because of the scale of these changes, the first few days after release may be slightly turbulent. While we have taken extensive precautions to minimise issues, some problems may still appear. If you encounter anything unexpected, please submit a bug report so we can investigate and resolve it quickly.
Houses
Head over the the Construction skill to get started.
Houses can be created by building a foundation.
Houses are built at the location your character is currently at.
Houses cost 25,000 gold.
Houses use the same dynamic system that powers guild halls, so players who run guilds will find the mechanics very familiar.
Build different structures to gain various boosts and quality-of-life improvements. For instance, constructing a Lumber Store can increase your maximum idle time for woodcutting.

The effects of the building are only applicable to the location the house is built in unless you purchase a Remote Conduit . For instance, without a remote conduit, you can only increase your maximum idle time at the location your house is built in.
Your house buildings don't stay in perfect condition forever. Over time, active components slowly degrade. If a component reaches 0%, the effects cannot be accessed.
While the buildings are in repair, they also cannot be accessed.
Check out the wiki for a more detailed explanation of how houses work.
House Guests

You can share your house with other characters (including your own alt characters) by building a Guest House. Please note that, due to the nature of this building, it is more expensive than other buildings.
Guests can only join a house one every 24 hours to prevent abuse.
More
Improved UX in the tavern on the apps.

Guild Conquest rewards have been updated so a character can no longer receive the same season shard reward more than once in the same zone after changing guilds. For new seasons starting on or after May 9, 2026, only that character’s best contribution will count for the reward, and older duplicate entries will show as Superseded.
Added the ability to view another character’s profile when inspecting a party.
Added "Food Used" to battle notifications.
Removed the snow map.
Players who reach level 100 in Meditation will now receive a free moving animated gradient.
Added rule 4.5 to clarify household trading.
Teleportation costs have been slightly reduced for most players to account for the newly added Construction level.
League rewards now only go to characters who contribute at least 1 point.
Added a "Getting Started" guide for new characters.
Changed the wording from "The game has been updated" to "Something has been updated".
Improved the friends list to make it easier to use, including the ability to pin friends.
Increased the membership item price to 50,000.
Added vendor price visibility on the market listing screen.
Bug Fixes
Fixed bug where viewing a zone from a past season showed Dominated or Contested instead of the guild that actually won that zone.
Fixed bug where past seasons could incorrectly show a live assault as active in a zone, even though that assault did not belong to the selected season.
Fixed bug where switching from a past season back to the current season left zone tags in the wrong state, showing winning guild or empty labels instead of the correct live conquest status.
Fixed bug that caused stamina to return as 1 at the end of a pet hunt.
Public API
Added evolution data to the pet public API.
Public pet API allows users to view other character pet inventories.
Fixed rounding bug for dungeon loot. This was a visual bug. It did not affect the game in any way and was isolated to the public API.
The public API now respects the characters pet inventory privacy setting and will return a 403 response if their inventory is closed.
Added location details to the character endpoint.
Removed happiness and hunger from the pet endpoint.

patchNotes.title: Membership Items
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.63.2-PB - Membership Items
patchNotes.excerpt: It's come to our attention that the use of membership scrolls has increased market activity significantly over the past few weeks. Due to their extremely low vendor value and high circulation, they are effectively bei...

contentBlocks.text: It's come to our attention that the use of membership scrolls has increased market activity significantly over the past few weeks. Due to their extremely low vendor value and high circulation, they are effectively being used as an alternative currency to reduce or bypass trade tax.

We haven't made any firm decisions yet, but we’re watching the situation closely and analyzing what it could mean for the economy long term. If it starts heading in a direction that feels unhealthy, we'll step in before it becomes a bigger problem.

The market tax is the primary way gold leaves the game, and if that system is weakened and left unchecked, gold can gradually inflate, pushing prices up and impacting everyone. Over time, this makes the entire economy harder for us to balance and maintain. The effects tend to build slowly, sometimes only becoming obvious years later, which is why it is important to for us step in early before the situation grows into something much more difficult to correct.

One of the options we're considering is gradually increasing the vendor sell value of membership items over time. That would naturally raise the tax impact when they're used in direct trades, which helps close the loophole without doing anything too heavy handed.

This is just a quick heads up to let you know we're aware of the trend and keeping a close eye on it. We haven’t made any firm decisions yet, but we felt it was important to flag it now so anyone involved in the market can factor this into their plans going forward.

As we've said in the past, the long term health of the game will always come first. We recognize the potential risks if this continues unchecked, and we want to make sure it doesn’t quietly grow into a larger issue over time.

blocks.text: It's come to our attention that the use of membership scrolls has increased market activity significantly over the past few weeks. Due to their extremely low vendor value and high circulation, they are effectively being used as an alternative currency to reduce or bypass trade tax.

We haven't made any firm decisions yet, but we’re watching the situation closely and analyzing what it could mean for the economy long term. If it starts heading in a direction that feels unhealthy, we'll step in before it becomes a bigger problem.

The market tax is the primary way gold leaves the game, and if that system is weakened and left unchecked, gold can gradually inflate, pushing prices up and impacting everyone. Over time, this makes the entire economy harder for us to balance and maintain. The effects tend to build slowly, sometimes only becoming obvious years later, which is why it is important to for us step in early before the situation grows into something much more difficult to correct.

One of the options we're considering is gradually increasing the vendor sell value of membership items over time. That would naturally raise the tax impact when they're used in direct trades, which helps close the loophole without doing anything too heavy handed.

This is just a quick heads up to let you know we're aware of the trend and keeping a close eye on it. We haven’t made any firm decisions yet, but we felt it was important to flag it now so anyone involved in the market can factor this into their plans going forward.

As we've said in the past, the long term health of the game will always come first. We recognize the potential risks if this continues unchecked, and we want to make sure it doesn’t quietly grow into a larger issue over time.

patchNotes.title: Guild changes and more!
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.63.0-PB - Guild changes and more!
patchNotes.excerpt: Guild Changes We’re making a small change in how we approach guilds. When the guild system was first introduced, we intentionally put a high cost on creating and maintaining a guild. The idea was to make sure guilds o...

contentBlocks.text: Guild Changes
We’re making a small change in how we approach guilds.

When the guild system was first introduced, we intentionally put a high cost on creating and maintaining a guild. The idea was to make sure guilds only existed when they had a clear purpose and commitment behind them. Over time, it's become clear that this approach is a bit too restrictive, especially for more casual players.
Our goal now is to make guilds more welcoming and accessible, mainly by lowering the costs to create and maintain them.

These changes also take future features into account, particularly housing. While housing is still in active development and no final resource requirements have been set, we want to avoid a situation where players feel forced to choose between investing in their personal house or supporting their guild. Reducing guild costs now helps remove that pressure before it ever becomes a problem.
As a result, we're making the following changes:
The guild creation cost has been reduced to 50,000 gold.
The mark cost for creating guild components has been reduced, along with the cost to repair them.
Quantity requirements for all guilds have been halved.
This should make it easier to start and sustain a guild, while keeping them meaningful as the game continues to grow.
Skin Chests

We feel like the skin system has been a bit underused, especially when it comes to collecting skins through normal gameplay. While museums help track your collection, acquiring skins almost exclusively through tokens has felt too restrictive. Tokens are already used for utility rewards, such as slots and the recently added character name colouring, which makes skin collecting feel like a trade off rather than something you naturally work towards.
We love collecting systems, and we want skin collection to happen more organically through playing the game. That’s where skin chests come in.

We’ve added support for skin chests that drop random character and background skins. These chests will be obtainable through gameplay, starting with dungeons, and potentially expanding to other areas like World Bosses in the future. They won’t be available for direct purchase from merchants.

When you open a skin chest, it rolls from all skins currently available in the merchants (including both token and shard merchants). Campaign skins are excluded. If you roll a skin you already own, you’ll receive shards instead. Shard rewards scale based on quality, ranging from 50 shards for standard skins up to 2,500 shards for mythic skins. For instance, if the chest rolls a mythic skin that you have, you will receive 2,500 instead.
Skin chests will begin appearing in dungeons over the next few days. There will be several different chest types, each with its own drop rates.

For full transparency, all odds for each chest will be fully visible on the item inspection page. Some chests will have a higher chance of dropping rarer skins, including Mythics. The museum will also list if the skin is acquirable via the chest or not.
Skins will still remain available in merchants if you’d rather purchase a specific one directly.

To be clear, these chests can only be obtained through gameplay or by trading with other players who earned them through gameplay. They cannot be purchased directly from the game. The chests will be tradable on the market at first, but we’ll be monitoring the economy closely. If they begin to cause issues, we may make them untradable later on.
Leagues
Leagues have been updated to use a fixed party size of 4 . This change addresses concerns around players being able to participate in multiple leagues at the same time.
Any new or existing leagues that are scheduled to start more than 2 days from now will be automatically updated to use the new party size of 4.
More
Increased username gradient edit time to 6 hours.
Added "Where to find?" tab for skins in the museum.
Fixed an issue where character health could be set to 0 when starting another action while in the middle of queued battles.
Fixed a bug that caused pets to be stuck in a characters showcase after being sold or traded.
Improved pet group UI.
Improved user onboarding when signing up for the first time.

patchNotes.title: Custom Name Colours
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.62.0-PB - Custom Name Colours
patchNotes.excerpt: Custom Name Colours Characters can now purchase a custom name colour. A solid colour slot costs 400 tokens. A gradient colour slot costs 700 tokens. Custom name colours are only active while an active membership is in...

contentBlocks.text: Custom Name Colours
Characters can now purchase a custom name colour.
A solid colour slot costs 400 tokens. A gradient colour slot costs 700 tokens.
Custom name colours are only active while an active membership is in place.
Colours must remain clearly readable and visible. If a colour is intentionally set to be difficult to read or invisible, the colour slot will be revoked without a refund.
Colours can be purchased on the character settings page.
More
The token conversion rate for the shrine has been increased to 900 gold per token, up from 700.
Fixed incorrect item effect listings on the inventory page.

Edit: This update mistakenly allowed existing username colours to be edited. This will be disabled after 5pm UTC (in around 1 hour). Please make any colour changes before this time, as editing will no longer be available afterwards.

patchNotes.title: Direct Trading and Beastmaster
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.61.0-PB - Direct Trading and Beastmaster
patchNotes.excerpt: Pet Trading Added the ability to trade pets directly. However, it's important to note that it comes with heavy limitations as to not undercut the companion exchange. Each pet has a minimum value based on its species,...

contentBlocks.text: Pet Trading
Added the ability to trade pets directly. However, it's important to note that it comes with heavy limitations as to not undercut the companion exchange.

Each pet has a minimum value based on its species, level, and evolution stage. When you give a pet in a trade, you must make a profit of at least the pets minimum value to cover the cost of the pet that would've otherwise been sold on the Companion Exchange.
For example, if you want to trade away a pet with a minimum value of 5,000 gold:
You give: pet (minimum value of 5,000 gold)
They must offer: at least 5,000 gold worth of items or gold
Your total profit must be 5,000 gold or higher.
More
Added Beastmaster class. This gives the character +10% Pet Mastery EXP and +10% Pet EXP.
Added a button on the league view to see your parties current progress in the league.
Fixed an issue that displayed an incorrect error message when feeding pets with no food.

contentBlocks.text: Snowball Fights!
Toss snowballs at other players during the active snowball fight window to earn points for your team.
View the list of scheduled battles on the campaign page.
Snowball fights only run during specific, short-lived time periods.
Any snowballs thrown outside of an active period do not count toward points.
Snowballs use separate limits from waving. You can throw one snowball every 30 seconds, and each player can be hit by a maximum of 100 snowballs within a 30-minute window.
Each snowball successfully thrown awards 1 point to your team.
More
Added a list of recent interactions to the profile page to reduce notification spam during snowball fights.
Fixed a server error that occurred when sending mail to a character with a close
Fixed the contest leaderboard so the Top 25 characters display correctly instead of showing all characters.
Get ready! The first snowball fight starts in around 10 minutes and will run for 1 hour. This gives us time to monitor things and make sure everything is working as expected.

patchNotes.title: Yule Fest
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.59.0-PB - Yule Fest
patchNotes.excerpt: @@IMAGE:Yule Fest The Yule Fest seasonal campaign is here! Craft snowballs, join snowball fights, and earn exclusive rewards in our festive Yule Fest seasonal campaign. Seasonal Contest (Beta) We're introducing a new...

contentBlocks.text: @@IMAGE:Yule Fest
The Yule Fest seasonal campaign is here! Craft snowballs, join snowball fights, and earn exclusive rewards in our festive Yule Fest seasonal campaign.
Seasonal Contest (Beta)
We're introducing a new seasonal mechanic to the game - seasonal contests.

When a seasonal campaign is active, you can participate in the contest at any time. When you join, you're randomly assigned to a team. Once you've been assigned a side, you're locked in for that campaign's duration. Remember to assign a team before you spend any points!
You can participate in one team per seasonal campaign. You cannot change teams once you've joined.
All characters in an account are automatically assigned to the same team.

All teams are competing to accumulate the most points before the campaign ends. There are two main ways to earn points for your team. You can contribute to the community goal, or you an claim campaign rewards.
The rewards at the end of the campaign is determined by your teams position at the end. A breakdown can be seen on the wiki.
This system is currently in testing and may be subject to change in future campaigns.
More
We've added a unique quest to the Yulewood Glades location. Check it out.
Added Lunark pet to the Celestial Exchange.
Updated the campaign UI.
Fixed iOS payments when Apple bundles a single order with multiple payments.
Fixed pet selection buttons incorrectly selecting pets that are hunting, battling, or sleeping.
Fixed a bug causing duplicate pet mastery effects.

patchNotes.title: Showcase, Wiki Search, and more
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.58.0-PB - Showcase, Wiki Search, and more
patchNotes.excerpt: Added item showcase slots to profiles. Free players can display up to 5 items, while members can display up to 10. Added the ability to view wiki results directly from the in-game search. Added the ability to mark you...

contentBlocks.text: Added item showcase slots to profiles. Free players can display up to 5 items, while members can display up to 10.
Added the ability to view wiki results directly from the in-game search.
Added the ability to mark your party as private to prevent other characters from seeing who is in your party.
Improved in-game notification when sending a pet to hunt in a location above your character’s combat level.

Pet nerfs! Oh no! We've noticed that pets were performing too well when many were sent to hunt at once, so the enemy-find timing has been tuned. While, we're not against the idea of pets being strong when playing strategically and utilizing them to their full, we feel there are still adjustments that need to be made so they don't overshadow other areas of the game. The range has shifted from 150s–50s to 200s–75s. Pets with low agility and movement now encounter enemies every 200 seconds instead of 150, while high agility and high movement pets now encounter them every 75 seconds instead of 50.
Pet mastery effects are now automatically applied to every pet without having to do it manually.
Daily rewards can now be redeemed even if your inventory is full.
Changed pet status timer to hh:mm:ss .
Equipping a bow now automatically replaces any items in the primary hand and off hand slots.
Fixed a bug that caused a pet to lose its evolution bonus when being sold on the companion exchange.
Fixed a bug that prevented the daily task counter from being displayed.
Fixed a bug that caused the temporary dismissal of the review box to not work.
Fixed a bug that prevented people from starting an action when activating auto daily reward claim and having a full inventory.
Fixed a bug that caused display issues on the promo codes box.
Fixed a bug that displayed a incorrectly formatted tooltip when hovering over a level element.
Fixed bug where the selected inventory item would not update after performing an action.
[Public API] Fixed upgrade_requirements not correctly displaying the hashed item ID when inspecting an item.
[Public API] Fixed an issue that resuled in stale content being served for world bosses.
[Public API] Fixed type casting for quantity and chance across various endpoints.
An accompanying update on iOS and Android also follows this release. Please make sure your apps are full up-to-date on the respective app stores. The latest versions are the following:
Android: v1.0.1.8 (it might take up to 24 hours for the update to appear on the Play Store)

patchNotes.bodyText:
Added item showcase slots to profiles. Free players can display up to 5 items, while members can display up to 10.
Added the ability to view wiki results directly from the in-game search.
Added the ability to mark your party as private to prevent other characters from seeing who is in your party.
Improved in-game notification when sending a pet to hunt in a location above your character’s combat level.
Pet nerfs! Oh no! We've noticed that pets were performing too well when many were sent to hunt at once, so the enemy-find timing has been tuned. While, we're not against the idea of pets being strong when playing strategically and utilizing them to their full, we feel there are still adjustments that need to be made so they don't overshadow other areas of the game. The range has shifted from 150s–50s to 200s–75s. Pets with low agility and movement now encounter enemies every 200 seconds instead of 150, while high agility and high movement pets now encounter them every 75 seconds instead of 50.
Pet mastery effects are now automatically applied to every pet without having to do it manually.
Daily rewards can now be redeemed even if your inventory is full.
Changed pet status timer to hh:mm:ss .
Equipping a bow now automatically replaces any items in the primary hand and off hand slots.
Fixed a bug that caused a pet to lose its evolution bonus when being sold on the companion exchange.
Fixed a bug that prevented the daily task counter from being displayed.
Fixed a bug that caused the temporary dismissal of the review box to not work.
Fixed a bug that prevented people from starting an action when activating auto daily reward claim and having a full inventory.
Fixed a bug that caused display issues on the promo codes box.
Fixed a bug that displayed a incorrectly formatted tooltip when hovering over a level element.
Fixed bug where the selected inventory item would not update after performing an action.

[Public API] Fixed an issue that resuled in stale content being served for world bosses.
[Public API] Fixed type casting for quantity and chance across various endpoints.
An accompanying update on iOS and Android also follows this release. Please make sure your apps are full up-to-date on the respective app stores. The latest versions are the following:
Android: v1.0.1.8 (it might take up to 24 hours for the update to appear on the Play Store)
iOS: 1.1.2

patchNotes.title: Performance Improvements
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.57.0-PB - Performance Improvements
patchNotes.excerpt: Significantly improved performance for low-end devices with a weak GPU. Fixed an issue that caused league contributions to not show correctly. The old wiki has been removed from the game. We've also taken some time to...

contentBlocks.text: Significantly improved performance for low-end devices with a weak GPU.
Fixed an issue that caused league contributions to not show correctly.
The old wiki has been removed from the game. We've also taken some time to improve the new wiki to make it easier to navigate.

What's Coming For the rest of 2025, our main focus will be stability, polish, and bug fixing. We want the game to feel smooth and consistent across the board. We’re not completely ruling out new features or content, but over the next few weeks our attention will be on improving the UX, UI, and the internal systems that keep everything running. Many of these improvements will happen behind the scenes, so you may not see patch notes for every change, but they should make the experience better.

We also have the Yule Fest campaign coming up (Friday 19th December), along with IdleMMO’s second birthday on December 6th. Make sure you log in on that day to claim a special Birthday Cake (Untradable) that gives powerful boosts. As a reminder, this year's celebration will not include a tradable birthday cake. The tradable cake was exclusive to the game's very first birthday.
Beyond that, we can look forward to Farming and Houses in 2026.

patchNotes.title: Improvements and Bug Fixes
patchNotes.headline: Version 0.56.0-PB - Improvements and Bug Fixes
patchNotes.excerpt: Added support for selecting multiple pets while they are hunting, sleeping, or battling. Added an option for members to automatically redeem the daily reward when performing an action. Added quick selection for pets t...

contentBlocks.text: Added support for selecting multiple pets while they are hunting, sleeping, or battling.
Added an option for members to automatically redeem the daily reward when performing an action.
Added quick selection for pets that are unhealthy or tired.
Significantly increased 30-day baseline rewards for all leagues. Since leagues vary in length, the payouts scale accordingly for those shorter than 30 days.
League reward shard floor increased from 500 shards to 2,000 shards (position 25 to 15)
Some leagues will receive a bonus to encourage more competition in leagues with lower participation.
Added the ability to assign colors to pet groups.
Fixed an issue where battle activity was tracking times incorrectly. ( Special thanks to Dravilea for investigating this thoroughly.)
Corrected the category mapping for pet hunt notifications.
Fixed a bug that allowed users to claim more ascension points than intended.
Added tracking metrics for pet hunting.
Updated the ordering of pet multi selection options to follow a consistent order across the game.
Fixed a broken image that appeared in game notifications.
Fixed an issue that caused duplicate enemies during power hunting.
Fixed "The Boars Challenge" dialogue.*
Fixed a UI issue on the idle action box that caused the element height to shift.*
Fixed various pet stats being incorrectly boosted without an effect attached to it.*
Improved visibility of the referral code on the Web App.
Fixed broken wiki links.
[Public API] Fixed X-RateLimit-Reset returning incorrect value.
* Some of the fixes above were already live for several days prior to this update.

contentBlocks.text: We're very happy to introduce the release of Version 0.55.0-PB. A huge update to IMMO that has just a little bit for everyone.
Pet Changes
Pet Hunting
You can now send your pets on hunts.
You can send up to 10 pets on hunts. This limit is separate from battling, so it's possible to send 10 pets on a hunt, and another 10 pets on battles.
The pets hunt until they run out of stamina (We'll get to that soon). No health is used when hunting.
The effectiveness of how quick they can hunt an enemy depends on two stats: agility and movement speed. Agile pets will bring back more enemies than slower ones.
Pet Status Rework
We've removed pet happiness and hunger.

We’ve added stamina to pets as an alternative way to reduce the number of pets being used across multiple characters. You can read more about this in the blog post. In short, stamina introduces a soft cap that lets us manage the amount of loot and actions a player can generate across all characters, without relying on strict hard limits. This approach feels more natural.
Stamina can be replenished by Sleeping. You must manually send your pet to sleep.
The better quality the pet, the more stamina it has and the more efficient it is at using that stamina.
Pet Evolution
When a pet reaches level 100, you’ll be able to evolve it.
Evolving gives the pet a 5% boost to every stat but resets it back to level 1.
A pet can be evolved up to five times, allowing for a maximum bonus of 25% across all stats, including important ones like movement and fatigue.
Pet Effects
We’ve reworked the system so that pets can now gain effects, just like characters.
There are currently two ways to get effects for your pet: a bonus from pet mastery, and patting your pet.
Patting your pet now gives your pet a +5% stat bonus for 2 hours in its stats.
Pet Exchange
You can sell your pets by listing them on the Companion Exchange.
Every pet has a minimum listing value, entirely dependent on the pet itself, which is directly tied to its rarity and quality.
The minimum listing value increases as the pet increases in level.
Pet listings are automatically removed after 3 months.
Shard Pets
You can purchase mythic pets at the Celestial Exchange merchants page for an extremely high shard cost.
The shard cost for the first mythic pet is set at 300k. We are introducing an offer of 250k for the first few months.
The pet will not appear immediately in the Celestial Exchange. It may take some time for it to appear.
More Changes
Hunger and Happiness has been removed.

We've updated the pet UI to feel more intuitive, especially when you are rotating your pets and sending them on different actions. It could get a bit overwhelming when you have multiple pets with different actions and statuses.
We've added the ability to multi-select pets so you can feed them, send them on battles, send them on hunts or send them to sleep, without having to do it one-by-one.
The introduction of the overview box which will give you a quick overview on your current pets including pending loot, pending enemies (from hunting), and more breakdown stats.
Everyone now gets a free standard pet. You can choose to decline this free pet if your slots are full.
Pet battle EXP range has been increased from 0.3 -> 2.5 to 0.5 -> 3.
Pet mastery bonus now accounts for the exponential nature of EXP. A breakdown can be seen in the wiki.
Quests
Quests are a brand new feature in IdleMMO that let you dive deeper into the lore, interact with NPCs, and take on different challenges.

One of our main goals with quests is to give items more purpose. Right now, many items feel a little scattered in terms of their uses. Quests give us a flexible way to fix that. If an item feels pointless, we can design a quest around it and instantly give it meaning.
Before starting a quest, you must talk to the quest giver and complete the dialogue.
Quests can distribute gold, items, and shards as rewards. The later quests distribute shards as a reward.
Each location has a quest completion requirement before you can unlock the quests. This prevents people from accessing the top quests immediately. You must start your quests at Bluebell hollow.
You can view the quest completion requirement breakdown on the wiki page.

Some quests have a quest line attached to them. Meaning, once you complete a quest, it will unlock another. But you will have to wait some time before you can complete the subsequent quests in the chain.
There are more than 100 quests. Some are lore building. Some are built for fun. Theres a mix of everything.
More quests will be introduced in the future.
Parties
Parties allow you to team up with other players.
You can invite other players to your party, or join up with your friends in their parties.
Right now, parties are exclusive to Leagues but this gives us room to add more mechanics to parties in the future.
Leagues
Leagues let you compete against other parties.

Each league focuses on a specific skill, and they run for different lengths of time. For example, there might be a Woodcutting League that lasts 14 days, where every party in that league competes to earn the most experience in woodcutting.
Leagues can last for a few days, two weeks, or even a full month. Each one is different.
The rewards depend on the length of the league. For instance, a league that is 30 days long will have better rewards than a league that is 14 days long.
Everyone in the party obtains the reward equally.
A league can also be isolated to specific classes. So, it's possible for a league to be specific to just classes like Cursed or Forsaken.
Few things to keep in mind:
The party leader has the option to withdraw the party from a league.
Once a party joins a league, no new members can be added.
Your party can join multiple leagues at once, but you can’t change your party until a league has ended.
You’re free to leave a party at any time, but you won’t be able to rejoin until that league has finished or if the party leaves the league.
Leaving the league removes all progress. Rejoining a league after it has been left will not return any progress.
UI Improvements
We’ve carefully reviewed the entire app and given it a complete makeover.
Most of the UI updates apply to the Web App, but the mobile app has also received some visual improvements.
More UI updates will be released in the future to ensure a consistent and unified look across the entire platform.

We’ve added new customization options, including the ability to move the hamburger menu (on the Web App for mobile devices) and adjust brightness and contrast for better visibility when dark elements don’t display correctly on your device.
Wiki
We've completely overhauled the wiki. The old wiki is still available, but it is slowly being phased out, and will be completely inaccessible in the future.
The new wiki can be accessed directly at https://wiki.idle-mmo.com
We've expanded on the wiki - adding more breakdowns, better details, and examples in various areas.
Lore
We've taken a substantial amount of time writing up the lore, making sure that the in-game actions and dialogues from quests match the overarching universe that is happening in the world of Valaron.
You can read the lore in the Wiki.
We will be continually adding lore to IdleMMO as the game matures and as we introduce more quests in the future.
Guilds
Guild officers can now schedule energizing pools.
We've doubled the effect of all guild weapons in the armoury.
Hunting
Your idle time for hunting is no longer limited by your Hunting Mastery level. You will now always hunt to the maximum idle time that your character permits.
Updated hunting UI to show you the subsequent enemies that are being hunted.
Purchase Orders
Removed 3 hours and 6 hours purchase order.
Default PO time is now 12 hours and no additional fee.
Reduced fee for 24 hours from +2% to +1%.
Reduced fee for 48 hours from +3% to +2%.
More
We've increased the maximum purchasable inventory slots to 21.
Updated the membership page to give a better breakdown on the membership benefits.
We've introduced changes that should make some pages feel much snappier.
The gold limit of market items has been increased to 100 million gold (from 10 million gold)
Removed the tavern experimentation notice.
Combat skill for dungeons is no longer used for the requirements.
Selecting a tag on the tavern now persists when you navigate back to the tavern at a later date.
Added the ability to search for characters when pressing on the "Trade" button on your profile, rather than having to navigate to the other characters profile.
Ascension level is now shown on the leaderboards.
Added notification number to the page title on the Web App.
Enabling auto-purchase now automatically sets the maximum to the maximum number according to the idle time.
Certain areas in the game are now locked out according to your characters total level. For instance, leagues can only be accessed when total level 150 or higher.
Added the ability to search for guilds in the global search.
Market listings are now automatically removed after 3 months. It may take some time for existing listings to be removed from the market.
Bug Fixes
Fixed a bug that prevented guild renaming from working on certain devices.
Fixed bug that prevented the creation of purchase orders for Dragon Soulstones.
Fixed missing commas on some numbers on the museum.
Fixed bug that displayed the incorrect time when repairing a guild hall.
Fixed inconsistency in specific circumstances where the rounding of numbers on the web app didn't match.
Fixed broken daily reward icon on the Web App.

Fixed a bug that removed a pet from the museum when releasing it. WARNING: Please ensure the pet is in your museum before releasing it as it needs to sync up. If you can see the pet in your museum, it's good to go. This only applies to pets hatched before v0.55.0.
Fixed bug that sometimes prevented the campaign page from being updated when switching between campaigns.
Fixed a bug that prevented you from scrolling to the bottom of the trade box.
Fixed a bug that allowed you to trade with yourself.
Fixed visual rounding bug on the battle breakdown when the hit chances was being incorrectly displayed.
[Public API] Fixed missing effects from potions.
[Public API] Fixed incorrect health
[Public API] Fixed error 500 status code when accessing the characters current action endpoint when in a world boss lobby.
Closing Statement
Due to the size of this update, it will likely introduce new bugs. Expect a few turbulent days while things settle and we roll out fixes for any issues that appear.
